PROSE:
The system interface slammed shut with a heavy, digital thud that echoed through the infinite white expanse. The *glitch* *locks* Artie's *stats* to a maximum of 1 HP and a 100% Critical Hit Rate, *finalizing* his *build* against his will. 

`[System Notification: Anomaly Integrity Breach. Build Finalized.]`
`[HP: 1/1 (Locked)]`
`[Critical Hit Rate: 100% (Locked)]`

"Cancel!" Fizz shrieked, her tiny, translucent hands flying across a holographic keyboard that materialized out of thin air. Her neon pink hair flared like a warning beacon as she hammered at the glowing keys. "Abort! Ctrl-Z! Undo!"

`[Error 404: Administrator Override Denied.]`

Artie stared at the floating blue text. The numbers didn't seem real. He was an accountant; numbers were his entire life. He knew how to balance ledgers, how to project quarterly losses, and how to spot a catastrophic deficit. Looking at his own life force quantified as a single digit was the ultimate deficit. 

"Fizz," Artie said, his voice terrifyingly calm. "What does one HP mean in this context? Is it a metaphorical one? Like, 'Number One in Health'?"

The pixelated fairy stopped typing. She slowly turned to face him, her digital blue eyes wide with panic. "It means if you trip on a root, you die. If a mildly aggressive bee stings you, you die. If you eat a slightly undercooked piece of chicken, your internal organs will rupture, and you will die."

Artie swallowed hard. He looked down at his chest. His Employee ID Badge still hung from the cheap nylon neck lanyard, the plastic casing slightly smudged from where he had pressed against the vending machine glass. He reached a trembling hand into his right pocket, his fingers brushing against the worn leather of his Leather Wallet. They were the only two things that had crossed over with him. A plastic card proving he worked for a mid-sized accounting firm, and a wallet containing exactly zero dollars and a punch card for a sandwich shop he would never visit again. 

"I'm going to die in a cheap suit," Artie whispered.

"Technically, you're already dead," Fizz offered unhelpfully. "But yes, your new physical avatar is going to die very, very quickly. I'm trying to open a support ticket with the System Admin, but the latency is—"

`[Warning: Teleportation Sequence Initiated.]`

The infinite white floor beneath Artie's feet began to vibrate. The pristine void fractured, black gridlines appearing across the space like a shattering mirror. 

"Wait!" Artie yelled, stumbling backward as a chunk of the floor simply ceased to exist, revealing a swirling vortex of binary code beneath it. "I'm not ready! I need a shield! Or a helmet! Or literally anything that isn't made of polyester!"

`[Destination: Tutorial Forest.]`
`[Transferring User: Artie (Anomaly)]`

"Hold on to something!" Fizz yelled, diving toward him and grabbing onto the edge of his neck lanyard. 

"There's nothing to hold on to!" 

The void collapsed. 

Artie didn't feel like he was moving; he felt like he was being compressed. The sensation was akin to being shoved through a dial-up modem. His vision inverted, colors bleeding into a blinding spectrum of neon static. He couldn't breathe. He couldn't scream. For three agonizing seconds, his entire existence was reduced to a stream of raw data violently colliding with the architecture of a new reality. 

Then, gravity returned with a vengeance.

Artie slammed hard into a patch of damp, spongy earth. The breath was knocked out of his lungs in a sharp wheeze. He squeezed his eyes shut, fully expecting a system prompt to announce his immediate demise from fall damage. 

Nothing happened. He was still breathing. 

`[Teleportation Complete.]`

He cracked one eye open. The blinding white of the void was gone, replaced by the deep, shadowed greens of a dense woodland. The air smelled of pine needles, damp soil, and the faint, ozone tang of static electricity. 

"Oww," Fizz groaned. The little fairy unentangled herself from his Employee ID Badge and floated upward, shaking her head to clear a halo of tiny, glitching stars that orbited her pink hair. "That was rough. The routing protocols for Anomalies are absolute garbage."

Artie pushed himself up onto his hands and knees. The dirt beneath his palms felt real. The rough bark of the massive trees towering over him looked real, even if the leaves near the canopy seemed to have slightly jagged, low-resolution edges when the wind blew. He patted his right pocket. The Leather Wallet was still there, a solid, comforting lump against his thigh. 

He climbed to his feet, brushing a layer of pixelated moss off his slacks. A gentle breeze rustled the branches above, dropping a single, perfectly rendered pinecone onto the dirt a few feet away. It was peaceful. It was quiet. 

It was utterly terrifying. 

Artie *spawns* in the *tutorial* *forest* with his *glitched* stats *locked*.
